w_controller.usage_details: Evaluated in adapt_step as an affine scalar combination v_t = w @ z_t + b for sigmoid gating, but as a fixed heuristic rather than an optimized parameter.

b_controller.usage_details: Bias scalar added in affine controller formula.

phase_12_as_run.forensic_question_answer: Why does Selective_state_adaptive contain 5 total parameters but 0 trainable parameters? In deltacore/streaming/models.py lines 888-895, w_controller and b_controller were registered as nn.Parameter with requires_grad=False and initialized to hand-tuned constants. In examples/phase_12_spatiotemporal_benchmark.py, no optimizer was created and no loss.backward() was ever invoked. The benchmark solely unrolled streaming evaluation via adapt_step(), which updates the associative state buffer M.data via online delta rules. Consequently, 0 parameters were trainable and 0 gradient steps occurred. The controller was purely an unlearned, fixed heuristic.

phase_12_1_corrected_and_trained.controller_learning_behavior: When given non-zero gradients and trained via backpropagation through time on the recurrent state stream, the 5 parameters adapt with delta_theta = 4.029. All weights become positive, driving the controller gate to high retention (alpha_t approx 1.0). The resulting evaluation error (0.95068) is statistically identical to fixed high retention (0.95070), demonstrating that learned state-conditioned modulation converges to static high retention on this benchmark.
